items.title: Not What a Child Expressed: Auditing the Sign-to-Text Safety Interface in Child-Facing AI
items.abstract: Automatic sign language translation (SLT) has entered consumer products, turning American Sign Language into English text for dictation, messaging, and queries put to a conversational assistant. Child-facing AI and platform trust-and-safety tooling decide on text, using filters on minor accounts and grooming classifiers that score chat messages. A signing child who uses SLT therefore reaches these safeguards through a translation. We found no publicly documented system in which the two have been jointly evaluated, and the leading deployed SLT model was neither trained nor formally evaluated on signers under 18. items.title: Appear2Meaning: A Cross-Cultural Benchmark for Structured Cultural Metadata Inference from Images
items.abstract: Museum records express how people understand heritage objects through cultural and historical relations. Recovering these human attributions from images is a technical challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We introduce Appear2Meaning, a cross-cultural benchmark of 750 museum objects for image-only recovery of title, culture, period, origin, and creator. Its evaluation framework distinguishes field-level from complete-record compatibility and uses human validation for semantic judgement. Across nine VLMs, mean field accuracy is 36.16--49.82%; 7.20--17.02% of records have all four contextual fields compatible, and 2.13--7.87% have all five, including title. items.title: Found, but Not Fixed : From Software Vulnerability Discovery to Fixes with Iterative LLM Pipelines
items.abstract: Software vulnerabilities persist as a critical threat despite the deployment of sophisticated detection tools and AI assistants. While detection has advanced, the subsequent code repair phase remains a primary bottleneck; manual intervention is inherently slow, costly, and prone to introducing secondary regressions and issues. In this paper, we investigate whether an iterative, LLM-based pipeline can provide a robust solution for the automated repair of vulnerable functions in real-world code. We propose a generalized framework that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs) through a multi-stage feedback loop. items.title: Set-based State Estimation for Unknown Dynamical Systems from Noisy Output Data with Probabilistic Guarantees
items.abstract: We develop a methodology for set-based state estimation from noisy input-output trajectories, without a predefined model structure for the unknown state dynamics or access to training state measurements. We derive a bound on the state set diameter that depends on the sensor map and leverage it as a surrogate to formulate a tractable linear program balancing state set tightness against output trajectory coverage. Combining this certificate with deterministic or probabilistically certified measurement noise sets and leveraging the results from scenario optimization with relaxation, we provide joint a posteriori probabilistic guarantees for state inclusion and state set diameter. Numerical simulations corroborate our developed theoretical guarantees.

items.title: Code-Anchored Review Feedback Improves Correctness and Lowers Hosted Editing Cost on Large R Files
items.abstract: Tokens drive the cost and latency of generative AI (GAI) code editing, and correctness decides whether an edit is useful. We study how the format of a reviewer's feedback, a human-AI collaboration (HAIC) channel, impacts both. In a paired experiment on 36 synthetic base-R tasks with seven models, the same requested changes were delivered as a holistic list (control) or as the export of FileMark (treatment). That code-review extension anchors each comment to the code it concerns and quotes it. items.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
items.abstract: Dysarthria reduces speech intelligibility, requiring self-directed rehabilitation based on fine-grained feedback to capture gradual articulatory changes. For Japanese speakers, such feedback is naturally provided in mora units due to its distinct moraic timing and consonant-vowel structure. While recent visualization methods have explored distance-based feedback, most are limited to vowels. Extending them to consonants is challenging, as generative embeddings often smooth transient spectral structures. We propose a visualization system for Japanese consonant morae that maps articulatory deviations onto a two-dimensional space defined by temporal and spectral distances from healthy reference speech. items.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
items.abstract: Estimating treatment effects is central to science across many disciplines and requires counterfactual reasoning about alternative worlds. In the real world, however, each unit reveals its outcome only under the factual world. Thus, the factual and counterfactual outcomes can never be jointly learned by any model trained on real data. The problem is therefore tractable only in synthetic settings, where both worlds can be generated. Recent progress on prior-data fitted networks (PFNs) has shown that models pre-trained purely on synthetic data can transfer to real-world prediction. items.abstract: Flow-matching robot policies generate each action chunk through repeated network evaluations, one per denoising step. We compare the two in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter world action model, on LIBERO-Goal. items.title: REFLEX: Reflexive Equilibrium Fixed-point Learning for Endogenous eXchanges
items.abstract: In over-the-counter corporate bond markets, dealers compete for client trades by quoting bid and ask prices. Tighter quotes attract more business, but also informed customers more likely to trade ahead of adverse price moves, leaving the dealer holding the risk. As dealers increasingly use machine learning to set quotes, they retrain these models on the trades their own quotes attract, creating a feedback loop in which each model reshapes the market that generates its next training data. The question is therefore not only whether a quoting model performs well, but whether the market it creates stays stable as the model learns from it. items.title: Minimax Estimation of Discrete Distributions under Hockey-stick Divergence
items.abstract: We initiate the study of estimating a discrete distribution with respect to the hockey-stick divergence from independent samples. We provide non-asymptotic upper and lower bounds on the minimax expected loss in terms of the alphabet size, the number of samples, and the divergence parameter. The upper bounds are achieved by add-constant estimators, while the lower bound is derived via a Bayes risk argument. Both upper bounds and lower bounds reveal a transition between polynomial and exponential regimes as the parameters of the problem vary.

items.title: SARL: Label-Free Reinforcement Learning by Rewarding Reasoning Topology
items.abstract: Reinforcement learning is critical to improving large reasoning models, but its success relies heavily on verifiable rewards (RLVR), making it hard to use in open-ended domains where correctness is ambiguous and cannot be verified. Moreover, reasoning trajectories remain largely unconstrained, and optimizing solely toward the final answer can favor early exploitation over generalization. items.abstract: With the advancement of AI technologies, Generative AI (GenAI) and human written text have become nearly indistinguishable. items.abstract: Agnostic learning has a well-developed theory of computational and statistical complexity. For learning with distribution shift, even the choice of an appropriate error benchmark remains challenging. items.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
items.abstract: LLM agents operating repeatedly in the same environment, such as a code repository, a database, or an application suite, encounter tasks that share latent structure. Experience can reveal this structure, allowing agents to reuse environment knowledge and learn from environmental feedback. Agents can adapt at test-time using this experience through two channels: retaining it in context and updating their weights. These channels are usually studied separately, leaving unclear what each contributes and when they complement each other. items.title: Controllable Generative Trajectory Prediction via Weak Preference Alignment
items.abstract: Deep generative models such as conditional variational autoencoders (CVAEs) have shown great promise for predicting trajectories of surrounding agents in autonomous vehicle planning. State-of-the-art models have achieved remarkable accuracy in such prediction tasks. Besides accuracy, diversity is also crucial for safe planning because human behaviors are inherently uncertain and multimodal. However, existing methods generally lack a scheme to generate controllably diverse trajectories, which is arguably more useful than randomly diversified trajectories, to the end of safe planning. items.abstract: Pretraining data curation decides what a model learns from, yet what makes a document worth learning from depends on what the model already knows. Influence-driven selectors already rank documents to improve one run; we argue that training-data attribution should steer pretraining by identifying testable data properties that become reusable curation criteria, evaluated on new data against cheaper selectors at matched total cost, discovery included. items.abstract: Influence-function-based methods like MAGIC provide exact first-order scores for trajectory data attribution, yet only retraining indicates whether those scores accurately predict data removal. items.abstract: How much must a predictor's scores change when a community's elicited fairness standard changes? items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.abstract: Agent harnesses have emerged as a promising mechanism for continual learning, alongside test-time parametric learning. However, the current benchmarks have several limitations: they generally focus on a single applied domain, serve each instance only once, and assume a single family of learner, so memory-based and weight-based systems are rarely compared on the same scale. We propose Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream built from the three ARC-AGI editions, whose tasks need no domain knowledge. items.title: RIFT: Reward Improvement Field Transfer for Cross-Domain Offline RL
items.abstract: Learning from limited target data is a central challenge in cross-domain offline reinforcement learning. Abundant source data can help, but dynamics differences can make direct transition reuse unreliable. items.abstract: Reinforcement learning can make automated red-teaming more successful while narrowing the attacks it produces. This experiment reproduces attack diversity reduction using three runs with a Qwen2.5-14B attacker and a Phi-4-mini defender trained by direct preference optimization (DPO). items.abstract: Surrogate models approximate the solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) for given geometries and boundary conditions. items.abstract: Stochastic closure modeling is an emerging area in reduced-order modeling of large and complex (e.g., multiscale, multi-physics) systems, for which the computationally affordable reduced-order physical descriptions (e.g., digital twins for additive manufacturing, world models for AI agents) in numerical simulations inevitably lead to information losses that cannot be well addressed by classical deterministic closures. items.abstract: Identifying tree species from bark photographs matters for forest inventory and the wood-processing industry, yet the design choices behind deep-learning approaches have not been studied systematically, and some reported results may be inflated by images of the same trunk appearing in both training and test sets. items.title: ExclaveFL: Verifiable Claims for Federated Learning using Exclaves
items.abstract: In federated learning (FL), data providers jointly train a machine learning model without sharing training data. This makes it challenging to provide verifiable claims about the trained model, e.g., related to the employed training data, data sanitization, or training algorithm---a malicious data provider can simply deviate from the correct training protocol without detection. items.abstract: Despite a known dependence between grokking and model parameter count, how model capacity shapes grokking remains an open question. items.abstract: Dataset distillation compresses a large training set into a compact synthetic set while preserving its downstream utility. items.abstract: The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into core business operations has created an urgent need for robust corporate governance infrastructures capable of managing complex ethical, legal, and operational risks. While organizations have increasingly adopted high-level AI ethics principles, a critical implementation gap persists: fewer than half of organizations that cite AI governance as a boardroom priority have a formalized governance framework in place. items.abstract: Test-time training (TTT) layers replace the linear fast-weight memory of modern recurrent architectures with a small neural network trained online by gradient descent. items.abstract: Dataset distillation compresses a large training set into a small synthetic set that preserves downstream training utility. items.abstract: AI agents often discover mid-execution that their plan is broken, for example when an action fails or a tool is withdrawn. items.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations can capture the nanoscale physics of fracture at the atomistic level, but their computational cost prohibits predictions at the length scales and time scales needed for many applications. items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have shown impressive capability to understand and develop code. items.abstract: Backdoor attacks pose a persistent security threat to machine learning systems, yet their behavior under graph continual learning (GCL) remains underexplored. items.abstract: Shapley-based measures are widely used for measuring variable importance in statistics and machine learning. items.abstract: Recent advances in speech technology predominantly favor high-resource languages, leaving speakers of Sub-Saharan African languages underserved. items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve high scores on medical benchmarks, but does this performance translate into reliable diagnosis as a conversation unfolds? items.abstract: Many decision-making problems involve multiple objectives, where actions affect several performance metrics, fairness criteria, or safety constraints. items.abstract: Whether a ductal breast lesion is called atypical hyperplasia or low-grade carcinoma in situ increasingly determines surgery. items.abstract: Tabular prediction has long been dominated by gradient-boosted decision trees and specialized deep tabular models, while large language models (LLMs) remain difficult to make competitive despite their cross-task adaptability and transparent reasoning traces. items.abstract: Training neural networks to simulate highly oscillatory wavefields presents optimization challenges, often hindered by spectral bias and poorly conditioned physics-based loss landscapes. items.abstract: The use of large language models (LLMs) to coordinate multi-agent teams raises a fundamental architectural question: whether task allocation should be centralized in a single LLM controller or distributed across autonomous LLM agents, particularly when communication is unreliable. items.abstract: We introduce NeSySy, a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that jointly produces logical constraints and consistent datasets. items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have been shown to exhibit strong Python preferences when generating project-level code, but there is currently no systematic way to measure this behaviour across new models. items.abstract: Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) is a widely used manifold learning technique for dimensionality reduction. items.abstract: Coding agents act on repositories through shell commands and file edits, and teams steer them with written engineering rules. Industrial settings expect such rules to be enforced and their application to be evidenced, and a rule given as prompt text provides neither. We test whether executable contracts enforced while the agent works reduce rule violations compared with the same rules in the prompt, retrieved as guidance, or checked only after generation. Violations are scored by an oracle whose methods differ from the in-loop checks, and the oracle is validated by two human reviewers and a model reviewer. items.title: Random Cut Forests, Games and Diffusion over Approximately Nested Anisotropic Local Geometry
items.abstract: Just as the data in a dynamic stream changes, questions asked of the stream also change in intent: what to hold constant, which counterfactuals to consider, and so forth. Energy-based learning has been celebrated for its uniform approach to losses and estimation, but interpretability remains challenging. Tree-based methods, on the other hand, offer high interpretability but often rely on bespoke, disjointed estimators. Neither paradigm readily supports changing questions on streaming data. items.title: Evidence-Conditioned Completion and Synthesis of Electronic Health Records
items.abstract: Patient information can guide electronic health record (EHR) generation, but how its amount shapes predictive utility and disclosure risk remains poorly characterized. Here we present EHRDiB, which unifies visit completion and synthesis by distinguishing original missingness from withheld inputs and combining a shared multimodal representation with an evidence-conditioned latent diffusion bridge. We compared EHRDiB with three completion and eight synthesis methods on MIMIC-IV and numerical and discretized Duke Health representations. items.abstract: PDE discovery aims to identify from data the governing law of a physical system. Constituting a cornerstone of scientific advancement, it has become during the past decade a major line of research in the rapidly evolving field of Physics-informed Machine Learning (PiML). Among the open problems to address in this domain, the post-hoc evaluation of discovered PDEs raises the particular difficulty of being multifaceted. items.title: SAMark: A Self-Anchored Text Watermarking with Paragraph-Level Paraphrase Robustness
items.abstract: Semantic-level watermarking (SWM) improves robustness against text modifications by treating sentences as the basic unit. However, robustness to paragraph-level paraphrasing remains difficult because such attacks globally disrupt watermark signals by changing sentence order. In this work, we propose SAMark, a self-anchored watermarking framework that removes the dependency on sentence order by establishing a step-independent green region in semantic space. items.abstract: A churn model is useful through the customers it selects for a retention offer: the better model is the one whose selection makes the campaign more profitable. items.abstract: Pretraining an encoder once and reusing it across tasks is a widespread approach in vision and language. items.abstract: Coding agents can synthesize and optimize code-based policies from simulator feedback, allowing the resulting program to act with zero inference model calls. We propose a framework that first develops competence by refining the policy through a feedback cascade, moving from episode returns to hierarchical goals and belief updates which can be scored densely from simulator. items.abstract: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. Incidents in 2025 and 2026, including prompt-injection attacks on coding agents and self-propagating supply-chain worms, show that this arrangement fails in predictable ways. items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) trading agents now trade stocks for their users, and benchmarks rank models by their agents' returns. Yet a single run's return says little about skill. In our study, two runs of the same model that differed only in the random seed ended 5.2 points apart on average, so telling skill from luck takes many backtests across markets, models and seeds. However, live arenas trade each day only once, and backtests either use the few months after a model's training cutoff or run on years the model may remember, often with news joined to prices by calendar date. items.title: Low-Altitude Fluid Antenna Network with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs) integrate terrestrial and aerial platforms to provide ubiquitous communication, sensing, and localization services for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and electric vertical takeoff and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. However, dynamic air-ground and air-air channels, abrupt blockages, and heterogeneous interference hinder the realization of this goal. Nevertheless, fluid antenna (FA), a cutting-edge multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technique, overcomes these challenges by reconfiguring antenna positions to unlock additional spatial degrees-of-freedom. In this paper, towards bringing low-altitude FA networks into reality, we study the fast and high-performance FA reconfiguration for low-altitude FA networks with multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL).

items.abstract: The Internet of Drones (IoD) needs secure telemetry and proximity sensing within the SWaP-C constraints. We show that a single blind neural receiver driven by one chaos-based waveform performs both functions without a separate radar transceiver. items.title: From Weights to Features: Sparse-Autoencoder-Guided Activation Regularization for Continual Learning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Weight-protecting regularizers such as elastic weight consolidation (EWC) are a standard defense against catastrophic forgetting; however, in the sequential fine-tuning of large language models, they exhibit a stability-plasticity tradeoff that penalty tuning cannot resolve. We attribute this limitation in part to polysemanticity: because each weight participates in many unrelated concepts, a per-weight importance score has difficulty isolating the knowledge that requires protection. items.title: Better Call Graphs: A New Dataset of Function Call Graphs for Malware Classification
items.abstract: Function call graphs (FCGs) have emerged as a powerful abstraction for malware detection, capturing the behavioral structure of applications beyond surface-level signatures. Their utility in traditional program analysis has been well established, enabling effective classification and analysis of malicious software. In the mobile domain, especially in the Android ecosystem, FCG-based malware classification is particularly critical due to the platform's widespread adoption and the complex, component-based structure of Android apps. items.abstract: Evaluating the quality of AI-generated clinical notes is hard: standard metrics like ROUGE measure lexical similarity to reference notes, while expert checklists encode what committees believe matters. Neither captures what clinicians actually complain about. Recent work has shown that evaluation criteria can be mined from user feedback and filtered to criteria that LLM judges can reliably enforce. We argue that this is where much of the value is lost. The criteria that fail enforceability are disproportionately the ones clinicians raise most often, because high-frequency complaints are stated as several questions glued together. items.abstract: We study when compositional structure yields dimension reduction in supervised learning. items.abstract: Neural networks with randomly generated hidden weights (RaNNs) have been extensively studied, both as a standalone learning method and as an initialization for fully trainable deep learning methods. In this work, we study RaNN expressivity for learning solutions to non-linear partial differential equations (PDEs). Despite their widespread use in practical applications, a rigorous theoretical understanding of the approximation properties of RaNNs in this context remains limited. items.abstract: We study the minimization of anisotropic exponential interaction energies over probability measures on the sphere, motivated by mean-field models of self-attention in transformer architectures. We further show that it is the only stationary measure with full support for the dynamics considered. We use the stochastic viewpoint to derive an algorithm for sampling from the minimizer. items.title: Too Good to Be Real? Diagnosing and Reducing the Gap Between AI Preference and Real User Engagement
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to generate and evaluate online content, yet it remains unclear whether the qualities they associate with higher engagement match what real users respond to. We introduce Ontological Preference Measurement, which represents answers along three dimensions: logic, affect, and expression. items.abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. items.abstract: Rough path signatures are a universal feature map for continuous paths and, via the expected signature, characterise path distributions. items.abstract: Self-attention has greatly contributed to the success of the widely used Transformer architecture by enabling learning from data with long-range dependencies. items.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves the reasoning capabilities of small language models through token-level teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories. items.title: Advancing ESG Intelligence: An Expert-level Agent and Comprehensive Benchmark for Sustainable Finance
items.abstract: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) criteria are essential for evaluating corporate sustainability and ethical performance. items.abstract: Callers to Arabic customer-service lines speak their own dialect, while speech recognizers are built and evaluated mainly on Modern Standard Arabic (MSA). items.abstract: In this paper we present the Formal Atlas, a system for the study of natural language semantics using proof assistants. Our aim is to formalize semantic accounts,   check their predictions and compare the implemented theories. items.abstract: Natural language autoencoders (NLAs) are a method for generating natural language explanations of LLM activations. We develop evaluations based on auditing tasks that test the ability of NLAs to surface latent knowledge, identify whether a model was misled by a hint, and catch a silent fabrication. items.abstract: A direction in a language model's hidden state can be used to probe whether a concept is present or to steer the model toward it. items.abstract: One way to study language-model introspection is to test whether models can identify where their activations have been perturbed. items.abstract: Sharpness Aware Minimization (SAM) updates model parameters using gradients evaluated at adversarially perturbed weights, but it remains unclear which aspects of this procedure are sufficient to reproduce its generalization behavior. items.abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. items.abstract: Random forests (RFs) often achieve high prediction performance, but their ensemble structure can be difficult to interpret.
